title: Certified backflow testing: verify the program requirement first
description: Certified testing means the issuing program accepts the tester, the specific assembly result, and the required filing evidence. A service-company claim or a passing field visit alone may not complete the program obligation.
prompt: What must be known before this work can be closed out?
answer: Certified testing means the issuing program accepts the tester, the specific assembly result, and the required filing evidence. A service-company claim or a passing field visit alone may not complete the program obligation.
urgency: Treat deadlines, active discharge, damaged bodies, critical service, or uncertain authority requirements as reasons to use a qualified path.
diagramAlt: Backflow service and compliance workflow reference
identifiers: Identify the exact assembly, model, size, and protected system.
Separate service work, certified testing, report submission, and approval responsibility.
Retain the final proof with the property asset record.

choices.label: I have a notice or program requirement
choices.detail: Use the issuing program to verify deadline and filing requirements.

choices.label: The assembly failed or needs service
choices.detail: Document the device and define repair plus retest scope.

choices.label: I manage a commercial asset
choices.detail: Separate access, shutdown, testing, and closeout responsibilities.

steps.title: Match the asset and requirement
steps.body: Record property, assembly, model, size, system use, program notice, and access conditions.

steps.title: Define the complete responsibility
steps.body: Confirm qualified service, testing, repair authorization, report submission, and approval ownership.

steps.title: Retain the closeout evidence
steps.body: Keep the final test, repair record, and official confirmation together for the next service cycle.

safeChecks: Confirm the official issuer and eligible tester requirement before booking work.
Use the exact manufacturer record for parts or assembly compatibility.
Keep both failed and completed records where retesting is required.
stopConditions: Do not assume a service visit includes a required filing.
Do not approve work without identifying the exact assembly and scope.
notThisDevice: A generic service listing does not establish program eligibility.
A device family is not enough to identify compatible parts.
This page does not replace a qualified assessment or authority approval.
evidenceNote: Use the exact manufacturer record and governing utility or authority instructions to validate the final path.
